answer: Neighborhood atlas anchoring. Each agent must be reachable through a bounded set of persistent neighbor links that other agents independently confirm; a new identity inherits the cheapest available position in that topology. An attacker cloning agents pays to acquire and hold distinct neighbor slots around real clusters, since unlinked clones sit in a whisper-thin fringe that routing ignores. Clusters that fall below a minimum confirmed-degree threshold lose haven status and their traffic share, so mass registration yields no visibility and costs sustained link maintenance per clone.
